overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance data reveals that space and planetary extreme what-if scenarios (particularly extreme environment scenarios involving rare materials, unusual physics, or hypothetical immersion like diamond and burning ice planets) are significantly outperforming standard psychological facts or traditional animal trivia in recent 7-day velocity and engagement. Videos utilizing 'What If You Fell Into...' hooks combined with high-value planetary anomalies generate the highest views-per-day and engagement ratios (likes-per-view).

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,028 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) published late September show vastly superior engagement compared to older standard static facts.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on hypothetical space scenarios that place the viewer directly into extreme, counterintuitive alien environments.

winning_patterns.pattern: High-Value Anomaly Hooks with Financial/Rarity Specifiers
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into This $26 Nonillion Diamond Planet?' (495 views, 23 likes) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (980 views, 21 likes) prove that combining astronomical anomalies with stark, mind-bending contrast captures high viewer retention and likes.
winning_patterns.action: Incorporate scale, extreme time dilation, or material value comparisons directly into the primary title and opening 3 seconds.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5 views) and 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' (38 views) show extremely low velocity and poor engagement over time.
weak_patterns.action: De-prioritize standard psychological illusion micro-facts unless framed through a groundbreaking, high-stakes neuro-tech breakthrough.

weak_patterns.pattern: Repetitive Direct Fact Restatements Without Narrative Arc
weak_patterns.evidence: Simple declarative statements like 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' or 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' suffer from flat view curves after initial seeding compared to active narrative 'What If' structures.
weak_patterns.action: Shift entirely away from simple declarative fact-stating toward narrative-driven environmental exploration.

next_video.concept: What happens if you fell into a rogue planet hurtling through interstellar space with zero sunlight and a nitrogen ocean?
next_video.opening_direction: Start in pitch darkness where temperatures drop instantly to absolute zero, challenging the viewer to imagine falling endlessly through an invisible atmosphere.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that despite being completely frozen and lightless, the subsurface ocean teems with hydrothermal energy capable of melting steel.
next_video.reason: Capitalizes on the proven high performance of 'What If You Fell Into...' space scenarios while introducing a fresh cosmic phenomenon (rogue planets with subsurface oceans) absent from historical uploads.
fresh_topic_constraints: Must not feature diamond planets, burning ice, or standard gas giants.
Must avoid recycling old titles or previously covered celestial bodies like TrES-2b or Venus.
Must maintain rigorous astrophysical accuracy while keeping the pacing ultra-fast.

experiment: A/B test a pure cinematic space what-if featuring an undiscovered rogue exoplanet against a high-contrast historical storytelling micro-drama to see if narrative history can match the current momentum of space hypothetical scenarios.
